facts.text: Six Senses Thimphu, Punakha, Gangtey and Paro lodges sit high on hilltops in Bhutan's western and central valleys.
facts.excerpt: Six Senses Thimphu, Six Senses Punakha, Six Senses Gangtey, and Six Senses Paro sit high on hilltops like gemstones throughout the Kingdom’s western and central valleys

facts.text: Six Senses Bumthang is located near the Chamkar Chhu river, further east.
facts.excerpt: while Six Senses Bumthang is located near the Chamkar Chhu (river), calling you further east.

facts.text: Guests can stay at one lodge or all five, and Six Senses plans a bespoke journey through the Kingdom.
facts.excerpt: Whether you stay at one lodge or all five, we will take care of all the planning for a bespoke “Khamsa” or “Royal Stroll” through the Kingdom.

facts.text: Journeys come with a private guide, driver and vehicle.
facts.excerpt: With a private guide, driver and vehicle, we’ll take you beyond the inspiring scenery and deep into the heart of each valley you explore.

facts.text: Accommodation is in villas and suites, including three-bedroom villas.
facts.excerpt: Six Senses resort in Bhutan offers 82 spacious villas and suites, starting from 645 square feet indoors for the suites and up to 3,681 square feet indoors for the three-bedroom villas.

facts.text: Experiences include a sunrise hike to Tiger's Nest and visits to Wangdecholing Palace Museum.
facts.excerpt: Hike at sunrise to Tiger’s Nest or wander through the history of the mystical Buddhist Kingdom at Wangdecholing Palace Museum.

facts.text: Guests can light a butter lamp during evening prayers at the 14th-century Damchen Lhakang.
facts.excerpt: Light a butter lamp during evening prayers at the 14th-century Damchen Lhakang.

facts.text: Guests can dine in the Chubjakha Ruin.
facts.excerpt: Dine in the Chubjakha Ruin and be immersed in feudal Bhutanese times.

facts.text: Yoga or meditation is offered at the lodge's Prayer Pavilion.
facts.excerpt: Start the day with yoga or meditation at the lodge’s Prayer Pavilion before heading out to visit Buddha Dordenma

facts.text: Six Senses Thimphu is in Babesa, Thimphu.
Bhutan lies high in the Eastern Himalayas between India and China.
facts.excerpt: Tucked high in the Eastern Himalayas between India and China, Bhutan is one of the world’s most enigmatic destinations

facts.text: Bhutan is described as the world's first carbon-negative country.
facts.excerpt: As the world’s first carbon negative country, Bhutan is a vibrant tapestry of protected forest and abundant nature

facts.text: Bhutan has chosen low-volume, high-value tourism.
facts.excerpt: Bhutan has chosen a path of low-volume, high-value tourism, preserving its pristine environment and rich cultural heritage.
